headline: A wallet is “wealth” plus “cloth” — a Japanese coinage found in texts from 1675.
“Cold” may be “claw” plus “painful”, with a missing i.
Hydrogen is “water element” — a word-for-word copy of Dutch, coined in 1834.
The youngest child is the “end child” — with a little clipped-off pause in the middle.
The word for an aunt is a “little mother” — and the kanji don't spell it that way.
A human being is, in Chinese, “people” plus “among”.
To refuse was originally to “split words”.
A doll is a “person shape”, and a native reading, built from hito and kata, says the same thing.
A meal, or cooked rice, with an honorific on the front.
“Quiet” is a bound root meaning “quietness”, plus a か that makes na-adjectives.
The usual reading of “disciple”, でし, is a shift from the older Chinese-derived ていし.
Three days out has its own word, and nobody is sure what its first syllable is.
An autograph, a sign and a sine all land on one katakana spelling.
A “beautiful person” has a native twin spelled the same way: “good-faced person”.
To be based on something is to “attach” to a “foundation”.
“Freedom” is an old Chinese word that Fukuzawa Yukichi repurposed in the 1860s.
“Tonight” was /kʲəm bʉan/ in its Chinese-derived reading, and became /kombaɴ/.
“Interesting” is literally “face-white”, with cousins in Okinawan and Miyako.
The “Messrs.” you write on a company envelope is an honorific stuck on the word for “inside”.
Good night is a polite “rest” — and the verb for rest began as an adjective meaning “easy”.
The card has two Japanese cousins: カルタ and カルテ.
“National language” also means Mandarin — but only in a Taiwanese sense.
“Very young” may once have meant “without a chief”.
“Grandmother” came from Chinese — but the ぼ in it is a change that happened inside Japanese.
“English” came from Chinese, or was assembled in Japan from “England” and “language”.
“One person” has a look-alike in Old Japanese: pi1dari, which became hidari.
“Wife” began, in Chinese, as a woman of the “room, chamber”.
Canned food is a “can stuffing”, with the つめ voicing to づめ.
A bar owner and a master of arts are the same English word — with an Italian twin.
“Temperature” is “warm” plus “degree”, and it appears in a text of 1837–1847.
A parcel is a “little package”, with つつみ voiced to づつみ.
